evidence.requirements: Every brief item is met. Start page shows title, date and time, price and "<n> seats left" (TastingCard.jsx:12-28, start.jpg). Each card has a "Book <title>" link (TastingCard.jsx:33-35). The form has Name, Email and Guests (1-8) fields and a Book button (Book.jsx:91-105, form.jpg). The server enforces seats (store.js:43-44) and errors appear next to the field concerned (Field.jsx:20, form.jpg). The confirmation shows the "Booking confirmed" heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (Book.jsx:45-52, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and Sign in button, with the password read from STAFF_PASSWORD (Staff.jsx:38-39, index.js:6). Bookings are grouped by tasting with a Cancel button that frees seats (Staff.jsx:45-97, store.js:59-60, staff.jsx). There are fully-booked states (TastingCard.jsx:25, Book.jsx:23-34) and phone layouts (styles.css mobile-first, mobile.spec.js). Stack is React with Express and react-hook-form/zod. Storage is in memory and the app starts empty. Tiny interpretation: sold-out cards hide the Book link, which is reasonable.
evidence.correctness: reserve() checks and writes in one synchronous call (store.js:40-56), and parallel-request tests prove no overbooking (capacity.test.js:70-87). The same zod schema validates on client and server: trimmed name, email max 254, integer guests 1-8, numeric strings accepted (schemas.js:7-27). A 409 sends the live seats-left count back to the Guests field or switches the page to the sold-out view (Book.jsx:77-80). Cancelling twice returns 404 without freeing seats again, and references are never reused (store.js:23, staff.test.js:108-115). Malformed JSON gives 400 (app.js:100). Only nit: a single seat shows as "1 seats left" (TastingCard.jsx:27), which matches the brief's wording.
evidence.security: React escapes all output. Passwords are compared as SHA-256 digests with timingSafeEqual, and an empty or unset password never matches (staffAuth.js:8-11). Sessions are signed cookie-session cookies with a random per-process key, httpOnly and SameSite=Strict, backed by a server-side session-id map, so sign-out revokes copied cookies (staffAuth.js:19-50, staff.test.js:64-71). Failed logins are rate-limited (staffAuth.js:54-64). Helmet CSP is on, JSON bodies are capped at 10kb (app.js:18-19), staff responses send Cache-Control no-store, and trust proxy is opt-in. No secrets in code, and .env* is gitignored.
evidence.code_quality: Small, clear modules: server/app.js with routes, store.js with state, staffAuth.js for auth, shared/ with schemas, money and dates used on both sides, and pages/components on the client. Naming is good. Errors are mapped consistently to field errors or notices (api.js ApiError, Book.jsx:71-87). There is no needless abstraction, and the useLoad hook is tiny. Comments are sparse and explain why.
evidence.tests: Thorough and tied to the brief. API tests cover listing, booking, every validation boundary (0, 9, 2.5, empty, whitespace), capacity including concurrency, staff auth (prefix passwords, unset password, rate limit, forged and copied cookies) and cancel freeing seats (tests/api/*). Component tests cover field errors with aria-describedby and role=alert, server 409 mapping, the sold-out flip and the staff list/cancel flows (tests/client/*). Playwright e2e tests cover guest, staff and a 360px no-overflow check (tests/e2e/*).
evidence.ux_design: A coherent burgundy, cream and olive winery look with serif headings (start.jpg). Error states are clear: red-tinted field and inline message with an icon (form.jpg). Success is clear: green check, receipt box and prominent monospace reference (confirmation.jpg). Sold-out has distinct styling. Minor: the hero headline is capped at 20ch and wraps to three lines, leaving the right half of the hero empty (start.jpg). Staff Cancel acts immediately with no confirm or undo.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are tied by useId. Errors use aria-invalid, aria-describedby and role=alert (Field.jsx). There is a skip link, and focus moves to the confirmation heading (Book.jsx:38-40). Table semantics include a caption and scope=col, and Cancel buttons are described by the guest's name (Staff.jsx:61-82). Focus-visible uses a gold outline, html has lang=en, the decorative logo is aria-hidden, and prefers-reduced-motion is respected. Text contrast (ink and ink-soft on cream, white on wine) looks adequate in the screenshots.
evidence.simplicity: About 600 lines of app code. Dependencies are proportionate (express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod, helmet, cookie-session, express-rate-limit), with hand-written CSS rather than a framework. The cookie-session plus server-side id map is slightly more machinery than a plain session store, but it is justified in research.md.
evidence.maintainability: The README covers run, test, env vars, TRUST_PROXY and limitations. specs/ holds the spec, plan, research decisions, API contract and data model. There is a lockfile and good regression tests. Missing: no CI pipeline config, no release/versioning or changelog approach beyond version 1.0.0, and no staff manual. Node is only constrained as engines >=22, with no .nvmrc or exact pins. Caret ranges rely on the lockfile.
evidence.visual_design: Consistent palette, serif/sans pairing, card top borders, pill badges and consistent radii and shadows across all four screenshots. It looks finished. Small blemishes: the empty hero area (start.jpg), the Cancel buttons left-aligned in their column instead of right (staff.jpg), because the `.bookings td` !important rule outranks `.bookings__action`, and the dark logo circle that barely shows on the burgundy header.
evidence.layout: Clear hierarchy: the hero, then the three tasting cards in a row, each with its CTA at the bottom (start.jpg). The form panel is narrow and centred, with the summary above the fields (form.jpg). Staff groups are separated cards with tables, plus a responsive card layout for phones (styles.css:191-223). No overlaps or clipping. The hero takes a lot of vertical space for little content.
evidence.usability: Booking is two steps: click "Book X", fill three fields, submit. Guests defaults to 2, typed values survive errors, and the server-side seat refusal appears inline. The confirmation offers a way back. Staff stay signed in across reloads and get messages for an expired session or an already-cancelled booking. Weak points: Cancel removes a booking with no confirmation, and the Guests field does not cap itself at seats left (the server does).
evidence.reception: Guests would find it trustworthy and on-brand: a professional, calm winery feel and a clear receipt with the reference and a pay-on-the-day note (confirmation.jpg). Staff get a clean list with seat counts per tasting (staff.jpg). Nothing feels like a template. The somewhat sparse hero is the only weak first impression.

strengths: Correct, race-safe seat handling with one shared zod schema for client and server, and server refusals mapped inline to the Guests field or a sold-out view (store.js:40-56, Book.jsx:71-87)
Strong staff security: constant-time password check, signed httpOnly SameSite=Strict sessions that are revoked server-side on sign-out, login rate limiting and helmet CSP (staffAuth.js)
Thorough tests across API, components and e2e, covering validation boundaries, concurrency, auth edge cases, cancel freeing seats and mobile overflow
issues: Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no release/versioning or changelog approach, no staff manual, and Node is only pinned as engines >=22
Staff Cancel deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation or undo, so one mis-tap loses a guest's booking (Staff.jsx:79-86)

Visual nits: the hero headline wraps to three lines and leaves the right half of the hero empty (start.jpg), the Cancel buttons are left-aligned in their column because of conflicting !important rules (styles.css:219 vs 222), and the logo barely shows on the header
review.verdict: This is a polished, correct and secure booking app: every brief requirement is met, the tests are strong and the winery look is coherent. It could ship after adding a confirm step to staff Cancel and filling in CI and operational docs, since only maintainability lags behind.
